craft_notes: Sthāyin: hinge-joy (the plea becomes the praise). Sanskrit: devī's imperative + bhairava's sādhu sādhu in one verse → L4 keeps both voices audible (turn at colon). Rows: row 6 (tradition-voice: sādhu kept as 'what you were asked'). Rupture: colon after entire — plea, then praise. Close: end-weight on essence (tantrasāra). Minimal pass: none. Read aloud: grace—cut— essence (the pivot sings). Rejected: splitting into two speakers' stanzas — killed: verse is one unit; 'gist' for sāra — killed: essence kept.

lines: Grant grace, O Lord — cut the doubt entire:
what you were asked, is the tantra's very essence.
l4.sanskrit_cite: prasādaṃ kuru me nātha niḥśeṣaṃ chinddhi saṃśayam | sādhu sādhu tvayā pṛṣṭaṃ tantrasāram idam priye

reads_against.argmap: How is the doubt cut? → The plea and the praise turn together: the doubt itself is the essence-question.
c1_essence: Grace cuts the doubt: what was asked is the tantra's essence.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with jijñāsā (wonder sharpened into seeking)
